pro-mustang-v1.purpose: Pixel 10 Pro XL (mustang) distinct OS signing setup: source definition only. Containers, access and one bootstrap run remain unbound.

access.policy: Access is checked live, not from recorded timestamps (owner decision 2026-11-03). After the signer login and under the lock, the run calls secrets describe and versions list on both secrets with the same credentials. If that first check fails (expiry, revocation, a missing get or list grant, a missing or occupied container), the run stops (metadata-unavailable, which with the gcloud executor also covers a missing container, or secret-occupied) before any key is generated or journaled, and nothing is used up. The same calls repeat just before the import; a failure there, or a denied version add, comes after the key exists and the journal is written, so it uses up the run (failed-before-commit or recovery-needed) and later runs refuse until the owner decides recovery. versions.add cannot be tested without adding, so the bootstrap grant must be one binding per secret holding secrets.get, versions.list and versions.add with a single expiry of at most 4 h, made at action time (a custom role like models-v0's roseosModelsBootstrapV1), and the run must be dispatched well inside its window. The time boxes (bootstrap access <= 4 h, an expiring secretAccessor) are enforced by the IAM conditions the admin sets and are not checked here; recorded expiries are optional and, when present, must leave minimumRemainingSeconds.

This is the retained existing pattern's public subject; no RoseOS or Frankel certificate subject is retained in this repository, so no match with the existing Frankel keys is claimed.
generation.note: Non-interactive form of generate-keys + encrypt-keys: make_key reads the passphrase from stdin and writes scrypt-encrypted PKCS#8 DER (it always exits 1 through its EXIT trap); the AVB key is generated with openssl genrsa 4096, its public key extracted by avbtool (which needs the unencrypted key, as in generate-keys before encryption), then encrypted with openssl pkcs8 -topk8 -scrypt using the passphrase file (encrypt-keys form); the unencrypted intermediate stays in the owner-only workspace and is overwritten and removed after encryption. Nothing runs until the installed tool identities are measured.
